title.analysis: Authentic title "Buying vs Leasing a Car: The “New” Reality in 2026" promises a current comparison. The script delivers a nine-year buy-vs-lease model, lease-payment mechanics, high-mileage and EV cases, and explains that "new" in quotes means the same trap re-priced. The title matches.

script.stored_text_completeness: All 18305 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored text ends on the closing line ("...the way the paperwork said it would.") with no sign-off; composites Odette, Barrett, Cyrus and Lorraine; minor ASR artifacts ("The That's", "three Townies"); audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: There's a silver crossover in your neighbor's driveway that's identical to yours. Same trim, same color, same week off the same lot. Nine years later, her driveway is empty and yours still has the car sitting in it with the title in a kitchen drawer underneath a pile of takeout menus. Here's the part that should bother you. She had the lower payment. Not by a little, by about $130 a month every month for nine straight years. She won
script.ending_words: from the bank shaking your hand. It's a Tuesday, your payment doesn't come out, and then the next month it doesn't come out again. That's what you actually bought, not a crossover. 4 years of a bill that never arrived. And that's the thing about your neighbor's empty driveway. It was never empty because anything went wrong. It's empty because everything went exactly the way the paperwork said it would.
script.analysis: Full 18305 canonical characters read. A single-narrator explainer with composites: two-driveway hook, 2026 price and debt context, the four-square sales sheet, lease mechanics (depreciation, residual, money factor, markups), the depreciation cliff, the nine-year Odette vs Barrett model, mileage overage (Lorraine), the EV lease case after the 45W credit ended (Cyrus), emotional cost, school promotion, incentive structure, three objections, and a decision rule. The arithmetic reproduces closely; the hook's "108 times" framing contradicts the model, and some market statistics are unverified.
beat_map: Hook: two identical crossovers, nine years.
What is "new": tariffs and the credit.
Close: the bill that never arrived.
